description: A generic list whose rows the reader can reorder: by pointer (through the shared pointer-drag helper), by keyboard, or from a per-row move menu that is the tap alternative WCAG 2.5.7 requires. The component never mutates the host's list — every committed move raises OnReorder with the indexes of the host's own Items, and the next render shows the order the host reports. While a keyboard move is in progress the rows are painted in the PENDING order, so the row visibly travels before it is committed; Escape or a release without a change paints the host's order again. Accessible model: role=list of role=listitem rows, each naming itself a localized "sortable item" and pointing at the hidden keyboard instructions; the row is the single focus stop of its pair (the decorative handle is tabindex=-1 + aria-hidden), Enter/Space grabs it, the arrows move it, Enter/Space drops it, Escape cancels, Tab cancels and leaves the list (never a keyboard trap), Alt+arrow moves one position without grabbing, and ONE polite live region narrates every step. Controls inside ItemTemplate keep their own keys.

typeParameters.name: TItem
typeParameters.description: The host's row model. The component never inspects it beyond KeySelector and ItemLabelSelector, so a record, a class or a struct all work.

parameters.name: AllowLocalReorder
parameters.description: Whether the reader may reorder the rows INSIDE this list. Default true. A host that only wants transfers between lists (a board whose column order means nothing) sets false: the keyboard grab/drop model and the per-row move menu are then not offered at all — a row that could be moved within its list but has nowhere to go would announce a change the host ignores — and the rows stop being tab stops while the pointer drag (and its cross-list transfers) keeps working. Such a list also renders no live region of its own. The host is then responsible for a per-row alternative.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the list. Null uses the localized default ("Sortable list").

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: DataTestId
parameters.description: Overrides the root data-testid; the default id is sortable-list and TestIdPrefix namespaces it.

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Disables every reorder path at once: the rows are no longer focusable, the pointer drag is not attached, no move menu is rendered and nothing is announced. The rows still render, so a read-only view keeps its content and its accessible structure.

parameters.name: EmptyContent
parameters.description: Rendered instead of the localized default ("No items to reorder.") when Items is null or empty. The hidden instructions and the live region stay rendered either way, so the list never loses its explanation.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: The cross-list drag group this list belongs to. Two lists that pass the SAME non-empty value accept each other's rows: a row dragged out of one and dropped over the other is reported as OnTransfer instead of a reorder. Null (the default) keeps the list on its own, exactly as before this parameter existed. The gesture itself is unchanged — the same sortable module over the shared drag helper; the group only tells it which sibling lists the pointer may leave the row in, and the module marks the list it would drop into with tm-sortable-list--drop-target.

parameters.name: HandleMode
parameters.description: Which part of a row starts a pointer drag. Handle (the default) attaches the drag to the decorative grip, so the rest of the row stays interactive; WholeItem makes the row itself the drag surface and requires a 400 ms touch long-press, so a tap and a page scroll still work. The keyboard grip is the row in both modes.

parameters.name: ItemLabelSelector
parameters.description: The word the live region and the move menu use to name a row ("Approve the plan moved to position 2 of 5"). Null falls back to the item itself when TItem is a string, then to the localized "Item {n}" with the row's position. The KeySelector is deliberately not a fallback: a database key read aloud ("3f2a… picked up") names nothing a person can recognise, and the menu trigger would carry it too.

parameters.name: ItemTemplate
parameters.description: The content of one row, rendered inside the row's labelled content element. Null renders ToString() of the item. Focusable content is allowed: the content element is fenced with @onkeydown:stopPropagation / @onkeyup:stopPropagation, so a link, input or button in the template keeps its own keys instead of grabbing the row, and in HandleMode=Handle the pointer drag starts on the decorative handle.

parameters.name: Items
parameters.description: The rows, in display order. The component renders exactly this order plus any pending keyboard move and never writes back to the list, so OnReorder is the only way a reorder becomes permanent. Null or empty renders EmptyContent (or the localized default) and keeps the instructions and the live region in place.

parameters.name: KeySelector
parameters.description: The stable identity of one row, used both for Blazor's @key — a reordered row keeps its DOM node and any child component instance instead of being re-created in place — and for the row's data-sortable-key attribute. Null falls back to the row's index, which is stable only while the order is stable, so a host that reorders should always supply this. Keys must be unique: if the selector repeats one, every row falls back to its index (a keyed diff throws on a duplicate sibling key, so a mistaken selector degrades to an unkeyed list instead of failing the render).

parameters.name: ListId
parameters.description: How the host recognises THIS list inside its Group — the value reported as SortableTransferArgs.ToListId when a row is dropped here, and as SortableTransferArgs.FromListId when one of this list's rows leaves. Null falls back to the component's own instance key, which is stable for the lifetime of the instance but meaningless to a host, so a group of lists a host has to tell apart should always set it.

parameters.name: OnReorder
parameters.description: Raised exactly once per committed move with the indexes of the host's Items list (FromIndex, ToIndex and the Source that committed it). Not raised when nothing moved: a grab that returned to its start, an Alt+arrow at the boundary, or a disabled list. The component does not reorder the list itself — the host applies the move and re-renders.

parameters.name: OnTransfer
parameters.description: Raised when a row of THIS list is dropped into ANOTHER list of the same Group. The component reports the move and changes nothing — the host removes the row from its own source collection, inserts it into the target one and re-renders. The component does NOT announce a transfer on its own live region: only the host knows whether the drop was accepted (a column at full capacity refuses it, for instance) and what the move is called, so the host owns that announcement and the surface keeps ONE polite region.

parameters.name: ShowMoveMenu
parameters.description: Renders the per-row move menu (Move up / Move down / Move to top / Move to bottom) that is the tap and mouse alternative to dragging. Set false only when the rows already offer their own reorder commands — a list without the menu and without a pointer has no way to reorder at all.

parameters.name: TestIdPrefix
parameters.description: Namespaces every internal data-testid of this instance as "{prefix}-{name}", so several sortable lists on one page stay targetable.

methods.name: OnSortableReorderCommitted
methods.description: The single commit path of the pointer drag (called from the module once per released gesture). Runs OnReorder with Source=Pointer. Not meant to be called by hosts — use OnReorder for the host side.

methods.name: FocusItemAsync
methods.description: Moves keyboard focus to the row at index of Items — the same index OnReorder reports, not a painted position. A host uses it for the focus hand-back after the control the reader was on is removed with its row (WCAG 2.4.3), so the reader lands on the row that took the removed one's place instead of on the document body. Returns whether a focus call was made: false means there was nothing to focus (the index is outside the list, the list is Disabled — a read-only row is not a tab stop — or no element was captured for that row yet).

examples.title: A plan whose steps the reader can reorder
examples.code:
@step.Title @step.Description
@code { private IReadOnlyList steps = [ /* ... */ ]; private void OnStepReordered(SortableReorderArgs args) { // The component never mutates the list: apply the single move yourself. var list = steps.ToList(); var moved = list[args.FromIndex]; list.RemoveAt(args.FromIndex); list.Insert(args.ToIndex, moved); steps = list; } }

examples.title: A whole-row drag list with a read-only switch
examples.code:
<TmSortableList Items="@columns"
                HandleMode="SortableHandleMode.WholeItem"
                Disabled="@viewOnly"
                KeySelector="@(column => column.Name)"
                OnReorder="@OnColumnReordered" />

notes: One reorder at a time: while a row is grabbed it owns the keyboard — the module stops the default action of the reorder keys on the row itself, Tab cancels the grab and moves the focus out, and Escape cancels the move, so a grab is never a keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2).
The pointer path rides the shared pointer-drag.js and pointer-gesture.js helpers — the module owns only the list geometry and the single commit, never a second gesture implementation.
Reduced motion suppresses the row transition in animations.css, so a reader who asked for less motion sees the rows snap instead of slide.

A transfer is reported ONCE, on the SOURCE list, and the component announces nothing for it: only the host knows whether the drop was accepted and what the move is called. A transfer-only list (AllowLocalReorder=false) therefore renders no live region of its own, so a grouped surface keeps ONE polite region.
